planting.note: Set divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Lilac Wonder flowers more freely and over a longer stretch than most border liriope, so give it a spot where the bloom spikes will actually be seen.

directions: Lilac Wonder is a free-flowering Liriope muscari selection whose glossy, dark green, ribbon-like leaves arch outward in loose clumps rather than standing stiffly upright, letting the dense spikes of rich lilac-purple flowers show clearly above the foliage in late summer into fall. It tolerates full sun, partial shade, and even fairly dry shade once established, making it more flexible about placement than fussier cultivars. Plant in well-drained soil and divide congested clumps every few years in spring to keep the bloom display strong. Its trailing habit and unusually long, dependable flowering window make it a good choice for edging paths or softening the front of a shaded border where flower color is the priority.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; the twisted foliage habit is a purely ornamental trait and needs no special care beyond standard liriope culture.

directions: Curly Twist is a novelty Liriope muscari selection grown for its spiraling, corkscrew-like green blades, a distinctive textural quirk that sets it apart from the straight, arching foliage of typical lilyturf cultivars. Deep lilac flower spikes rise above the twisted clumps in summer, followed by the small black berries typical of the species. It grows and divides like standard Liriope muscari, tolerating a wide range of light from full sun to fairly deep shade and adapting to most well-drained garden soils. Use it as a conversation-piece accent in containers or along path edges where its unusual foliage twist can be appreciated up close, rather than as a large-scale mass groundcover.

common_name: Green Midget Dwarf Lilyturf (Compact Solid-Green Liriope)

planting.note: Set divisions on tight centers in spring in well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Green Midget's small mature size means it needs noticeably less spacing than standard Big Blue-type liriope.

directions: Green Midget is among the smallest-growing Liriope muscari selections, forming tight, low tufts of solid deep green, unvariegated foliage well under a foot tall. Unlike the similarly small but silver-edged Silver Midget, its plain green blades give it a cleaner, more uniform look when massed as a fine-textured edging or foreground planting. It shares the standard species' tolerance for a wide range of light and average garden soil, and its diminutive scale means clumps can be set closer together than full-size liriope for a quicker, denser fill. Divide crowded clumps in spring every few years to maintain its neat, compact habit.
